headline: The vendored framework moves to 0.21.8, which turns TLS certificate compression off by default and reports a truncated HTTP response body as an error
summary: The vendored framework moves from 0.21.6 to 0.21.8. The store needs no code changes for it. The changes that affect the store's outbound requests and its logs are listed below.

items.title: Vendored framework refreshed to 0.21.8
items.body: Advances the vendored framework from 0.21.6 to 0.21.8, verified against the pinned ML-DSA-65 signing key before unpacking. Changes the store inherits without code changes: outbound TLS connections, including the Stripe, PayPal and webhook requests, no longer offer TLS certificate compression, so a server or an on-path attacker cannot reach a decompressor before the certificate chain is verified; a response body that ends short of its Content-Length, or an HTTP/2 stream reset before the body ends, now rejects with the transient http-client/truncated-body instead of resolving with a short body; a TLS session is resumed on a host that has both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses; the router, error-page and shutdown log lines replace token-shaped values (long hex strings, UUIDs, base64 and similar tokens) with [redacted]; and the vendored @blamejs/pki moves to 0.9.10.
